proposals.relationship: McGirr challenges Hofstadter’s psychological characterization of conservatism through the social history of successful modern suburban activists.
proposals.evidence_note: Own Suburban Warriors introduction, printed 7–8 in the licensed updated-edition publisher excerpt, names Hofstadter’s persecution/paranoid-style interpretation separately from Bell and Lipset’s status-anxiety claims. She credits their attention to ordinary adherents but argues that an excessively psychological framework obscures the Right’s modern social base and durability. This is her attributed historiographical objection, not an independent audit of Hofstadter’s originals, a claim that every conservative was rational, or a denial of conspiratorial rhetoric, which she discusses at 6–10. The introduction’s endnotes are not included in the excerpt and remain unread; no original Hofstadter title is guessed.
